newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures stay narrowly mixed late.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures stay narrowly mixed late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained narrowly mixed late Friday in sluggish trade, with prices still holding recent technical ranges and opinions mixed about the market's next move, industry sources said.
At 1425 EDT, November eased 0.6 cent to $2.365 per million British thermal units, while December was two cents higher at $2.54. Others were still narrowly mixed.

"The bears are having a little fun right now, and near-term the market could come off a little more, but there's some weather uncertainty and that should support the market," said one Houston-based trader.

While storage operators have made decent progress in building stocks for winter, most agreed they will be cautious about drawdowns early in the season after last year's cold forced inventories down to critically low levels.
Traders said this should keep operators in the cash for any early incremental demand and buoy physical prices near-term.
"I don't see us cratering right now. Storage players are going to guard inventories for a while," one trader said.
Technically, traders still pegged key support in November at $2.30, with resistance seen at Wednesday's high of $2.59 and then in the mid-$2.60s.

Cash sources said weekend Gulf Coast prices were off more than a nickel Friday to the low-$2.30s. Midcon pipes lost almost a dime to the low-teens. New York city gate gas was talked several cents higher in the high-$2.60s.
NYMEX said 17,625 Hub contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas was still 1.5 cents lower at $1.055, while most deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 95 Alberta contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
NYMEX November Permian natgas edged up one-half cent to $2.06, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 15 Permian contracts traded at 1355 EDT.
On the KCBT, November was one-half cent higher at $2.115, while deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 25 cents (NYMEX premium).
